answer: Ephemeral Task Binding: each agent identity is tied to a unique, time-limited task token derived from live sensor data—say, a violet pigment reading from the orchard's soil probe. The token is valid only once: completing the task consumes it and publishes an unlinkable proof, so replaying it fails. An attacker must pay to deploy fresh physical sensors and wait out each token window per fake identity, costing hardware and latency that scale linearly with sock-puppet count.
